network.tdhConsolidation.metadataDescrip: Combine up to four wallets you own into one collector on 6529: your TDH adds up, sets count across wallets and your vault can stay cold. Follow the guided signing steps.
network.tdhConsolidation.title: Combine your wallets
network.tdhConsolidation.lead: Most collectors use more than one wallet: a vault that stays cold, a wallet for trading, a hot wallet for signing in. Combining them tells 6529 they all belong to you, so they count as one collector.
network.tdhConsolidation.nothingMoves: Nothing moves. Your NFTs stay in the wallets they are in.
network.tdhConsolidation.limit: Combine up to {limit} wallets. The fourth requires fresh links from {date}; Guided Setup opens signing ten minutes later.
network.tdhConsolidation.figure.label: Up to four of your wallets count as one collector
network.tdhConsolidation.benefits.title: Why combine
network.tdhConsolidation.benefits.descri: What changes once your wallets count as one.
network.tdhConsolidation.benefits.cold.b: Sign in, vote and post with your hot wallet. Everything in your vault still counts, and the vault never has to connect.
network.tdhConsolidation.benefits.tdh.bo: TDH from every wallet counts toward one total. TDH gives your votes more weight in waves and counts toward your level.
network.tdhConsolidation.benefits.sets.b: Cards spread over several wallets count toward full sets, seasons and the Genesis, Nakamoto and Gradient boosts.
network.tdhConsolidation.benefits.move.b: Moving a card between your combined wallets keeps its holding time, so its TDH keeps building.
network.tdhConsolidation.benefits.old.ti: Keep the TDH of old wallets
network.tdhConsolidation.benefits.old.bo: Stopped using an old or exposed address? Combine it and its TDH keeps counting while you never connect it again.
network.tdhConsolidation.benefits.collec: Your wallets share one profile. Your cards are counted together on your profile, on the leaderboards and for Meme Card subscriptions.
network.tdhConsolidation.wallets.title: Which wallets to combine
network.tdhConsolidation.wallets.descrip: Combine the wallets you already use, up to four. If you are starting fresh, three is enough: a vault, a transaction wallet and a social wallet.
network.tdhConsolidation.wallets.vault: Holds your NFTs and never connects to anything, not even this site. Ideally a SAFE or a hardware wallet.
network.tdhConsolidation.wallets.transac: Buys, sells and trades on recognized marketplaces. It can also handle your vault's paperwork, so the vault never has to sign.
network.tdhConsolidation.wallets.social: Your hot wallet. It signs in to 6529, votes, posts, mints and pays for subscriptions, and holds no NFTs.
network.tdhConsolidation.wallets.old: Optional. A burned or exposed address you no longer use. Combining it keeps its TDH counting.
network.tdhConsolidation.wallets.more: Read the full safe collecting setup
network.tdhConsolidation.steps.title: How to set it up
network.tdhConsolidation.steps.descripti: The guided setup tells you which wallet signs next. Each wallet signing for itself can approve its links in one transaction; managers approve one transaction per link.
network.tdhConsolidation.steps.list.body: Open the guided setup and enter the wallets you want to combine, up to {limit}. If you are already combined, your current wallets are filled in for you.
network.tdhConsolidation.steps.sign.body: Switch to the wallet shown and approve its transaction. Each costs a normal network (gas) fee. A vault with a manager stays disconnected: its manager approves one transaction for each link.
network.tdhConsolidation.steps.done.body: Your profile shows the combined wallets within minutes. TDH fully updates at the next daily update, at 00:00 UTC.
network.tdhConsolidation.steps.order: Follow the order shown. Signing out of order, old return links or separate manager transactions can temporarily split your wallets, and votes you have cast in TDH waves can be reduced.
network.tdhConsolidation.before.title: Before you start
network.tdhConsolidation.before.keys: Every combined wallet can sign in as your profile, change your primary address and choose where airdrops go. Only combine wallets you control.
network.tdhConsolidation.before.merge: Profiles merge for good. If more than one of the wallets already has a profile, they become one. The handle and picture come from the profile with the highest CIC.
network.tdhConsolidation.before.public: Combining is a public record. Anyone can see which wallets are combined. It does not move your NFTs or let one wallet trade another wallet's cards.
network.tdhConsolidation.change.title: Changing it later
network.tdhConsolidation.change.add: Add a wallet: run the guided setup again. Your current wallets sign first and the new one signs last.
network.tdhConsolidation.change.remove: Remove a wallet: the leaving wallet can revoke its links in one batch transaction. Its manager revokes one link per transaction.
network.tdhConsolidation.change.lost: Lost or hacked wallet: from each of your other wallets, revoke the link to it straight away. Until the last link is revoked, it can still sign in as your profile.
network.tdhConsolidation.change.full: Already have four? Remove the old wallet first, then add the new one.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.title: Questions
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.cost.title: What does it cost?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.cost.body: One network (gas) fee for each transaction. Combining four wallets takes four transactions, or a few more if a manager signs for your vault.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.move.title: Do I need to move my NFTs?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.move.body: No. Your NFTs stay where they are. Combining only records that the wallets belong to the same collector.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.limit.title: How many wallets can I combine?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.limit.body: Up to {limit}. A fourth wallet counts only with links signed from {date}. Before then, a consolidation holds up to three.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.friend.titl: Can I combine with a friend or another collector?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.friend.body: No. Combining is for one collector's own wallets. Every wallet becomes a key to the profile, and combining different people's TDH is against the rules.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.before.titl: I set up four wallets before the start date. What now?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.before.body: Your consolidation keeps three of them. From {date}, run the guided setup with all four wallets. It signs again the links the fourth wallet needs.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.profile.tit: Which profile survives when wallets join?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.profile.bod: The profiles merge permanently. The handle and picture come from the profile with the highest CIC, then the highest TDH.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.order.title: What happens if I sign in the wrong order?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.order.body: Your wallets split into smaller groups until the last signature lands, and votes you have cast in TDH waves can be reduced. They are not restored, so cast them again once the group is complete. The guided setup only lets the right wallet sign each step.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.see.title: Where can I see my combined wallets?
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.see.body: Your profile's Identity tab lists them. On the TDH page, Explain my TDH shows every wallet that counts, and the Wallet Checker shows the links between any wallets.
network.tdhConsolidation.faq.expiry.body: No. A link lasts until one of its wallets revokes it.
network.tdhConsolidation.under.title: Under the hood
network.tdhConsolidation.under.descripti: The exact rules, a signing-order simulator and the security analysis behind the four-wallet design.
network.tdhConsolidation.design.metadata: The rules behind 6529 wallet consolidation, a signing-order simulator and the tested security analysis of the four-wallet design.
network.tdhConsolidation.design.title: How wallet consolidation works
network.tdhConsolidation.design.intro: The rules, the transactions and the analysis behind the four-wallet design, including what it protects against and what it does not. From {date}, a consolidation can hold up to {limit} wallets.
network.tdhConsolidation.design.guideNot: You do not need any of this to combine your wallets.

network.tdhConsolidation.rules.title: The rules
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.descripti: Consolidations are registered on the NFTDelegation contract. 6529 reads those registrations and groups the wallets.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.pairs.bod: Each pair of wallets registers a Consolidation (use case 999) in both directions, on Any Collection or The Memes. Two wallets need 2 registrations, three need 6 and four need 12.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.limit.bod: A consolidation holds up to {limit} wallets. A fourth wallet counts only when its links to the other three were registered in both directions on or after {date}.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.newest.bo: Wallets are grouped from confirmed links, newest first. If a member completes a link with a new wallet, that newer link moves it out of its group. This is how you leave a group or pair a wallet with a different one.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.collector: Every wallet in a consolidation can sign in as the profile, set its primary address and redirect its airdrops. Only consolidate wallets you control. Combining different people's wallets is against the rules.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.expiry.bo: Consolidation registrations do not expire. A link lasts until one of its wallets revokes it.
network.tdhConsolidation.rules.effects.b: Holdings across the wallets combine for TDH, including full sets, seasons, Genesis/Nakamoto and Gradient boosts, and transfers between them keep their acquisition time. The wallets' profiles merge permanently: the handle and picture come from the profile with the highest CIC, then TDH. Changes reach TDH within minutes and fully at the next 00:00 UTC snapshot.
network.tdhConsolidation.add.title: Add a wallet in four transactions
network.tdhConsolidation.add.description: Each wallet signing for itself can batch its links in one transaction. A Delegation Manager sends one transaction per link. Existing wallets sign first and the new wallet signs last; this avoids an intermediate split when the new wallet has no existing return links.
network.tdhConsolidation.add.step1: Wallets A, B and C each register one link to D, in any order, after the activation cutoff. Nothing changes yet.
network.tdhConsolidation.add.step2: D signs last, with one batch to A, B and C. The group becomes four wallets in one step.
network.tdhConsolidation.add.why: Signing D first, renewing existing return links or sending D's links as separate manager transactions can split the group temporarily. Each split re-runs the profile merge, and TDH-wave votes above the temporarily lower TDH are reduced and not restored.

network.tdhConsolidation.order.title: Try the signing order
network.tdhConsolidation.order.descripti: Wallets A, B and C are already consolidated and D is joining. This example assumes D has no existing return links and each wallet signs its own links in one transaction. Choose the order to see the groups after each transaction.
network.tdhConsolidation.order.pick: Choose the next wallet to sign
network.tdhConsolidation.order.signerA: Wallet A: one link to D
network.tdhConsolidation.order.signerB: Wallet B: one link to D
network.tdhConsolidation.order.signerC: Wallet C: one link to D
network.tdhConsolidation.order.signerD: Wallet D: one batch to A, B and C
network.tdhConsolidation.order.safe: No temporary split. A, B and C stay together, and D joins with the last transaction.
network.tdhConsolidation.order.unsafe: The group split in {count} of {total} steps before D joined. Each split re-runs the profile merge and can reduce TDH-wave votes.
network.tdhConsolidation.order.note: This simulation uses the same grouping rule as the backend: newest confirmed link first, every member linked both ways, up to four wallets.
network.tdhConsolidation.remove.title: Remove or replace a wallet
network.tdhConsolidation.remove.leave: A wallet you still control leaves with one batchRevocations transaction that revokes its links to all the others at once.
network.tdhConsolidation.remove.replace: To replace a wallet in a group of two or three, add the new one first, then remove the old one, so the group never gets smaller. A group of four is full: remove the old wallet first, then add the new one. The other three stay consolidated in between.
network.tdhConsolidation.remove.lost: If a wallet's key is lost or compromised, every remaining wallet revokes its link to it, one transaction each. Send them back to back: the removed wallet keeps access to the profile until the last revocation lands.
network.tdhConsolidation.remove.split: When a consolidation splits, the newest valid primary-address delegation that is at least 50,400 processed Ethereum blocks old (roughly seven days) decides which part keeps the profile. Otherwise the part with the most TDH keeps it, with the previous primary address breaking a tie. Changing the primary address still takes effect when processed.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.title: Why every pair: the alternatives we tested
network.tdhConsolidation.why.description: Asking every pair to link both ways costs a few transactions. Cheaper rules were modelled and tested before choosing.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.table.capti: Rules considered for the fourth wallet
network.tdhConsolidation.why.rule.majori: Linked both ways with any two members
network.tdhConsolidation.why.rule.fanout: Links to all members, one member approves
network.tdhConsolidation.why.problem.maj: Two of your wallets could add an outside wallet without the third.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.problem.fan: One wallet's key, or one transaction it was tricked into signing, could add an outside wallet to your full consolidation without anything visibly changing.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.problem.sin: The same weakness, and linking a member with a new wallet would pull the new wallet in instead of moving the member out, changing what that action means today.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.matrix.titl: Who can add an outside wallet to your consolidation?
network.tdhConsolidation.why.matrix.desc: An attacker owns an outside wallet and can make some of your wallets sign. The table shows whether the outside wallet can join your full consolidation, found by trying every set of registrations those wallets could sign.
network.tdhConsolidation.why.matrix.capt: Whether an outside wallet can be added, by rule and by how many of your three wallets an attacker controls
network.tdhConsolidation.why.conclusion: Every pair is the only rule where no subset of your wallets can add an outside wallet, and where every member follows the same rule. The cheapest alternative saves two transactions, once.
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.title: What consolidation protects, and what it does not
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.adding: No subset of your wallets can add an outside wallet: every existing wallet has to sign, and so does the new one.
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.old: Old registrations cannot fill the fourth slot. Links registered before the start date never form a group of four.
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.keys: It does not make any one wallet safer. Each wallet in a consolidation is a full key to your profile: if one is compromised, the attacker can sign in, change the primary address and redirect airdrops, whatever the consolidation rule. Four wallets means four such keys.
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.manage: A delegation manager (use case 998) can register and revoke consolidations for the wallet that appointed it. If one manager acts for all your wallets, that manager's key is enough to change your consolidation.
network.tdhConsolidation.protects.lock: A vault can refuse new consolidation links, including ones its manager sends, by locking use case 999 on Any Collection. It has to unlock before its consolidation can change.
network.tdhConsolidation.start.title: Why the fourth wallet has a start date
network.tdhConsolidation.start.body: Some wallets registered consolidation links long ago, for other reasons. If the limit had simply changed, those old links could have formed groups of four the moment it did. Counting a fourth wallet only for links registered from {date} means every group of four is set up on purpose under the new rule. Requiring both directions means an old one-sided registration cannot be completed by the other wallet alone.
network.tdhConsolidation.start.data: On {snapshotDate} there were {total} consolidations of two or more wallets: {two} of two and {three} of three. With the start date, none of them change when the limit rises. Without it, {ungated} would have changed straight away.
network.tdhConsolidation.tested.title: How it was tested
network.tdhConsolidation.tested.port: The backend grouping code was copied into a test harness and checked against all {total} live consolidations, with identical results.
network.tdhConsolidation.tested.exhausti: Each rule was checked exhaustively: every set of registrations an attacker controlling some of your wallets could sign, and every order in which a new wallet's transactions can land.
network.tdhConsolidation.tested.properti: Property tests check that {graphs} random wallet graphs group exactly as before when no registration is after the start date, and that {sequences} random register-and-revoke sequences keep the stored links consistent.
